subject: Dedicated capacity — budget anchors & GPU preference check
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@novumai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity — post-call recap + numbers we discussed

Hi Lena — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we can lock the estimate before next week’s procurement review.

What I captured from our conversation:
- Workload: customer-facing assistant with mixed generation + retrieval; avg response ~180 tokens; 40% of requests are short (<40 tokens).
- Target latency: 300–500ms p95 for short responses; comfortable up to ~1.2s on longer tails.
- Monthly volume (QL estimate): 50–120M generated tokens/month initially, with 3x growth over 12 months if adoption goes well.
- Success metric: keep marginal inference cost under ~$1,500 per 1M generated tokens as a target budget anchor.

We discussed dedicated reservation vs. hosted burst. To make the pricing concrete I attached two scenarios (spreadsheet) and pasted the headline anchors below. These are conservative, pre-ANS (auto-batching/kv-cache) savings.

Scenario A — H100-heavy reserved (higher throughput, higher baseline commit):
- GPU: H100 80GB (4x) reserved pool
- Effective throughput (avg): ~1.3M tokens/min per GPU (approx; depends on sequence mix)
- Monthly reserved nodes: 4 GPUs -> sustained capacity for peak windows
- Unit economics: estimate ~$1,100 per 1M generated tokens (includes reserved amortized + infra + support)

Scenario B — A100 80GB (balanced cost/throughput):
- GPU: A100 80GB (3x) reserved pool
- Effective throughput: ~0.9M tokens/min per GPU
- Unit economics: estimate ~$1,350 per 1M generated tokens

Scenario C — L4 inference-optimized (lower-cost, lower-capacity):
- GPU: L4 (6x) with autoscale for spikes
- Effective throughput: ~0.45M tokens/min per GPU; heavier batching needed
- Unit economics: estimate ~$820 per 1M generated tokens but with higher latency tail risk on long responses

Key tradeoffs we need your help on to finalize the quote:
1) Preference of GPU family (H100 vs A100 vs L4) — L4 can hit lower $/1M but may need more engineering guardrails for latency-sensitive UX.
2) Reserve size target: are you comfortable committing to a 3–4 GPU pool initially, or do you want a smaller reserve with burst credits?
3) Budget band: you mentioned a mid-year target of $1,200 / 1M as a soft cap — confirm if that’s a hard constraint for procurement.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm preferred GPU family and whether procurement wants a smaller 1–2 GPU pilot reserve or go straight to 3–4.
- We provide a formal reserved pricing quote and a 60-day pilot pricing addendum for evaluation.
- Call with procurement (if helpful) to walk the workbook and show how autoscaling/burst would work operationally.

Attachment: redwood_dedicated_pricing_scenarios_v1.xlsx (worksheets: assumptions, per-gpu-breakdown, 12mo-cost-model)

If you want, I can also include a per-route SLA uplift that adjusts price by +12% to guarantee 200ms p95 for short responses.

Thanks,
Camila
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124

Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — post-call recap + numbers we discussed

Hi Camila — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from procurement and infra: 

- Our initial procurement window needs a 12-month committed cost envelope. Optics matter: fingers-crossed we want to keep below $1,200 / 1M tokens if possible.
- We are biased to H100 for first phase because our RL/finetune cycles and some evals already run there; ops prefers homogenous fleet.
- For go-live we expect 60–90M generated tokens/month (not including embeddings or rerank calls). Growth model is the same (+~3x over the year).
- Can you show an amortized example with a 3-GPU H100 reserve and a separate example that starts at 1 GPU H100 + burst credits? Procurement will compare both.

We are available for a 30-min pricing review on Wednesday; invite procurement and infra.

Best,
Lena
Head of Product, NovumAI
lena.ortiz@novumai.com

Lena — perfect, I’ll prepare two concrete line-item quotes for the Wednesday slot:
- Quote 1: 3x H100 80GB reserved (monthly amortized + on-call + 99.9% SLA uplift option) — price target: ~$1,040 / 1M tokens (we can hit this with a 12-month commit + small onboarding credit).
- Quote 2: 1x H100 reserved + burst credits / auto-burst policy (pay-as-you-burst) — blended estimate: ~$1,380 / 1M tokens for the first 3 months while adoption stabilizes; drops toward ~$1,100 if you convert to 3x reserve by month 4.

I included a third note on L4 as a cost-saver alternative if you want to run non-latency-critical routes there — happy to add that as an appendix.

Meeting: I’ll send a Calendly invite for Wed 11/4 10:00am PT unless you propose another time. Ben, Marissa — can one of you join to cover discounts/commit terms and technical SLA options?

Thanks — sending the updated workbook and a short blow-by-blow for procurement before the call.

Camila
